<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-summary">Summary</button></h2><div id="work-acc-summary" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Ghaṭakarparakāvya is a romantic Sanskrit poem consisting of 22 verses. It tells the story of two lovers, Mādhava and Kalyāṇī, who face various challenges in their quest for happiness. The first verse introduces the couple and sets the tone for the poem. It reads &quot;Kalyāṇyā ca kṛtārthasya mādhavena saha priyaḥ,&quot; which means &quot;Kalyāṇī and her beloved Mādhava, who have found fulfilment in each other.&quot; As the poem progresses, the couple faces obstacles such as the disapproval of their families and societal expectations. Despite these challenges, they remain committed to each other and their love. In the end, their dedication to each other is rewarded, and they are able to overcome all the obstacles to their happiness. The poem ends with the couple living happily ever after. Overall, Ghaṭakarparakāvya is a beautiful example of Sanskrit poetry that celebrates the power of love to overcome adversity.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contents">Contents</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contents" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Ghaṭakarparakāvya is a romantic Sanskrit poem consisting of 22 verses. The poem tells the story of Mādhava and Kalyāṇī, two lovers who face many challenges in their pursuit of happiness. Verse 1 introduces the protagonists and their love for each other, with the line &quot;Kalyāṇyā ca kṛtārthasya mādhavena saha priyaḥ&quot;.<br><br>Verses 2-6 describe the beauty of Kalyāṇī and her affection for Mādhava, with lines such as &quot;Uddīpta mukhīṃ dṛśām&quot; and &quot;Samṛddhaśobhāsu divyāsu nityaṃ saṃgamaḥ&quot;.<br><br>Verses 7-11 describe Mādhava’s financial success and his return to his hometown to reunite with Kalyāṇī, with lines such as &quot;Dharmavṛttaṃ patijyeṣṭho rājadhānīṃ praveśitaḥ&quot;.<br><br>Verses 12-16 describe the wickedness of Mādhava’s stepmother and her attempts to separate the couple, with lines such as &quot;Kāryākāraṇasaṃgatiravasthā bhinnāti vā&quot;.<br><br>Verses 17-20 describe Kalyāṇī's banishment to the forest and Madhava's determination to follow her, with lines such as &quot;Vanāntare vanaṃ vṛkṣaiḥ saṃdṛśyātmānam ekaṃanayat&quot;.<br><br>Verses 21-22 describe the couple's reunion in the forest and their happiness living together in peace, with the final line &quot;Sugātraḥ sukhadaḥ santo yūthapekṣo mahābhujāḥ&quot;.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-uniqueness">Uniqueness</button></h2><div id="work-acc-uniqueness" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Ghaṭakarparakāvya is a unique Sanskrit poem that stands out for its simplicity and brevity. With just 22 verses, it tells the story of two lovers, Mādhava and Kalyāṇī, who face societal and familial obstacles in their quest for happiness. What makes the poem unique is its focus on the relationship between the two lovers, rather than external factors such as wars, kingdoms, or gods. It celebrates the power of love to overcome all obstacles and the endurance of love in the face of adversity. Despite its short length, the poem conveys a powerful message about the resilience and dedication of true love.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contribution">Contribution &amp; Notes</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contribution" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Ghaṭakarparakāvya is a significant contribution to Sanskrit literature, as it showcases the beauty and power of the language in its poetic form. The poem is unique in its brevity and simplicity, which sets it apart from many other Sanskrit works. Additionally, it offers a valuable insight into the society and culture of ancient India, particularly the norms and expectations surrounding romantic relationships. Its celebration of love as a universal force that transcends societal barriers and challenges is a timeless message that continues to resonate with readers today. Ghaṭakarparakāvya is a remarkable work of literature that enriches the canon of Sanskrit poetry and reflects the timeless human experience of love and its endurance.</div></div></div>
